Let’s dive into Chapter 8: Mastering the Buying Cycle—Timing, Triggers, and Momentum.
So, even if you’ve built great relationships and your solution fits perfectly, there’s one factor that can make or break your deal: timing.
Every organization has its own unique buying cycle. It’s kind of like a winding path through the woods—sometimes you breeze through sunlit clearings, other times you hit dense patches where everything slows down.
Your job? Figure out exactly where your client is on that path and give them just the right support at every step.
Let’s break down the typical stages of a buying cycle:
First, there’s Awareness—that moment when the organization realizes there’s a need, or maybe a new opportunity pops up.
Next comes Evaluation. Here, folks gather information, compare their options, and really start weighing the possibilities.
Then it’s Decision time—the group chooses a solution and works on getting it approved.
And finally, Implementation—the fun part, where your solution gets rolled out and integrated into their world.
Now, here’s where things get interesting: at each stage, you’ll find different stakeholders stepping up. Maybe during evaluation, the technical team wants to dig into the details. But when it’s time to implement, the end users have a lot more to say.
If you want to truly master the buying cycle, try these strategies:
Start with open-ended questions. Find out where your client is in their process—don’t just guess.
Think ahead: what are the usual roadblocks at each stage? Be ready with resources and answers when they pop up.
And sometimes, a gentle nudge—like sharing a case study or offering a pilot program—can keep things moving.
Here’s a real-world example: imagine a software company that keeps seeing deals get stuck after the evaluation stage. Instead of pushing harder, they offer a no-risk pilot. Suddenly, clients get a taste of the benefits, and making a decision feels a whole lot easier.
The big lesson? Momentum is everything. If things start to drag, check in with your stakeholders. Remind them what’s at stake, reconnect with their motivations, and look for new ways to add value. Sometimes, just recapping the progress or sharing a fresh perspective can reignite excitement.
As you guide your client through each stage, here are a few gentle reminders:
Be patient—don’t rush, but don’t disappear either.
Keep an eye out for any shifts in priorities or new faces that could impact timing.
And don’t forget to celebrate each milestone along the way—not just the big win at the end.
When you get in sync with the rhythm of the buying cycle, you’re not just selling—you’re guiding your client from the very first conversation all the way to a successful launch.
